issues.claim: "No portal, upload, checklist or status page, no practice-management tool"
issues.problem: The site-side absences (portal, upload, checklist, status page) are verifiable, but 'no practice-management tool' is a claim about the firm's internal back office that no cited source supports. Practice-management systems (Clio, MyCase, etc.) are not normally embedded in a public brochure site, so their absence from the HTML proves nothing.
issues.fix: Limit the factual statement to what was observed and flag the rest: "No portal, upload, checklist or status page on the site; we could not tell what back-office system, if any, runs the files." Then let the time-saving estimate stand as a range to be checked in the walkthrough.

issues.claim: "chasing documents and updating buyers, sellers and agents runs through two phone lines and a Gmail inbox"
issues.problem: This is an inference about internal workflow written as an observed fact. The only verified facts are the published contact channels (two numbers, a fax, a Gmail address). The firm may well coordinate by email from a different mailbox or by phone; nothing cited shows how a file is actually run.
issues.fix: Reframe as inference: "If files are coordinated the way the site suggests - through two phone numbers and a Gmail address - then document chasing and status updates are manual." Add it to the 'worth checking together' question on file workflow.

issues.claim: "recurring questions get answered live on two phone lines"
issues.problem: Same pattern as above: the site shows no FAQ and only phone/email channels, but nothing cited shows that recurring questions are answered by phone rather than by email or by an existing handout the firm gives clients.
issues.fix: Say "the site answers none of the recurring closing questions - no FAQ, no checklist - so they have to be answered one-to-one" and treat the phone-only channel as an inference.

issues.claim: "runs closings remotely by Remote Online Notarization"
issues.problem: The homepage says the office *can* "orchestrate signings from afar using Remote Online Notarization". The audit turns a stated capability into current practice.
issues.fix: Write "says it can handle signings remotely via Remote Online Notarization", or "markets remote signings".

issues.claim: "Fits what you use: WordPress, Gmail, the calendar."
issues.problem: WordPress and Gmail are verifiable from the site; no source identifies which calendar or mail/calendar platform the firm uses (a Gmail address does not establish Google Calendar, and a consumer Gmail address may not be the case-management inbox).
issues.fix: Drop "the calendar" or write "...and whatever calendar the office already runs, to be confirmed".

issues.claim: "no published hours" (audit body and founder email)
issues.problem: True of the firm's own site, but an unclaimed third-party listing (Birdeye) does publish Mon-Fri 9:00-5:00. Read literally, the sentence could be contradicted by the founder in the first reply.
issues.fix: Add the qualifier: "no hours published on the site", and in the email: "no hours anywhere on lozitolaw.com".
